finding: The harness surfaces the live 403 as a profile-permission problem with the exact required wording and click path, exits 4, and never retries into it. Verified by assertion AND by driving the CLI directly, not by trusting the test name.
evidence: Offline probe with cli_anything.zoho.utils.zoho_backend.requests.get patched to the recorded 403 body {"code":"NO_PERMISSION","details":{"permissions":["Crm_Implied_Api_Access"]},...}. Observed: `--json leads list` -> exit 4, requests.get call_count 1, type profile_permission_denied, httpStatus 403, zohoCode NO_PERMISSION, details verbatim, no rows key. `--json selftest` -> exit 4, call_count 1, status 'blocked', httpCode 403, leads null, deals null. Text mode -> exit 4, one Error: line + one Fix: line, no traceback. Every message begins 'profile permission not granted — this is a Zoho-side setting, not a credential problem'; every fix carries 'Setup → Security Control → Profiles → the connected user's profile → Developer Permissions → enable Zoho CRM API Access'. Control case: a 403 with code INVALID_REQUEST -> exit 1, type auth_error, profile message ABSENT — so the harness cannot cry 'profile' at an unrelated refusal. TestProfilePermission asserts the same across leads list, deals list, fields Leads, leads get, deals get with get.call_count == 1 each. No live Zoho call was made; the 403 was replayed from the recorded body.
fix: None needed on the code. The block itself is a Zoho-side account setting and is HALT: only Steven can enable the profile permission. Until he does, the honest live result of selftest is exit 4, status blocked.

finding: Three of the seven harnesses cannot be installed or tested in a clean environment. They declare cli-anything-browser>=1.0.0, which is not on PyPI and is not vendored in this repo, and they import cli_anything.browser at module level — so the dependency is required at import time, not just at call time. Their verification is inherited from an earlier engineer's venv that already had it; I could not reproduce it here.
evidence: `pip install ./homes/agent-harness` (and showingtime, showami) -> 'ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement cli-anything-browser>=1.0.0 (from versions: none)', exit 1, for all three. Installed with --no-deps, `cli-anything-homes --help` -> exit 1, ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cli_anything.browser', raised at homes_cli.py line 25 'from cli_anything.browser.core import fs as fs_mod'; identical for showingtime and showami. pytest then aborts at collection: '2 errors during collection' (test_core.py and test_full_e2e.py) for each. Their own TEST.md Part 2 headers already say the run was made with 'cli-anything-browser 1.0.0 and mcp 0.9.1 already present'. MAC-SETUP.sh lines 548-563 git-clone HKUDS/CLI-Anything and pip install browser/agent-harness into ~/Applications/CLI-Anything/.venv, so this is a documented, automated prerequisite rather than a package defect. I did not fetch the upstream repo (external code fetch, outside this pass's remit).
fix: No code change. Install the browser harness into the same environment first — MAC-SETUP.sh already does this on the Mac. The three packages' install/--help/pytest rows stay UNVERIFIED in this sandbox and must be re-run on the Mac after MAC-SETUP.sh. A prerequisite note was added as Part 4 of each of the three TEST.md files so the next engineer does not repeat the dead end.

finding: All seven packages DO carry a tracked .gitignore, in two slightly different generations. Build residue was present but untracked, and has been stripped. Correction to my own mid-pass reading: I briefly recorded four .gitignore files as missing and overwrote them — that was wrong and has been fully reverted.
evidence: `git ls-files integrations/cli-anything-harnesses | grep gitignore` lists all seven. Two generations: homes, showingtime and showami use 'build/, *.egg-info/, __pycache__/, *.pyc, .pytest_cache/'; skyslope, zipforms, lofty and zoho use the broader 'build/, dist/, *.egg-info/, __pycache__/, *.py[cod], .pytest_cache/'. Mid-pass, a presence check reported the latter four as absent from disk and I copied the narrower homes version over them; `git diff` then showed the overwrite dropping 'dist/' and narrowing '*.py[cod]' to '*.pyc' — a regression, not a fix. I restored all four with `git checkout --` and confirmed the working tree now matches HEAD for every .gitignore. The most likely cause of the bad reading is concurrent modification of this working tree by another engineer's session (integrations/omniroute-failover/README.md and claude-auto.sh went from clean to modified during this pass, which I did not touch). Build residue (build/, *.egg-info/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, *.pyc) was present in all seven, tracked in none — `git ls-files ... | grep -cE 'build/|egg-info|__pycache__|\.pyc'` returned 0.
fix: No .gitignore change shipped — the four are back at HEAD. The remaining inconsistency (two pattern generations) is cosmetic and was deliberately left alone rather than churned during a concurrent session. All build residue was stripped from all seven packages and the throwaway venv deleted. If anyone wants parity later, widen the three narrower files to the broader set, not the other way round.

finding: No `act` command group exists in any of the seven packages, and the browser backend's click/type_text are never imported. Confirmed statically for all seven and on the rendered help output for the four that run here.
evidence: `grep -w act` over the --help output of cli-anything-zoho, -zipforms, -lofty and -skyslope returned no match in every case, while the substring 'act' does occur in each (in 'action group', 'interactive', 'redact', 'redacted') — 2-3 occurrences per package. Word-boundary behaviour checked explicitly against the known trap: `echo my-listing-activity | grep -qw act` does NOT match, while `echo '  act  Do a thing' | grep -qw act` DOES — so the check still catches a real act group. Statically across all seven: no `def act` and no click command or group named 'act'; the only occurrences of act/click/type_text in non-test source are the FORBIDDEN_NAMES deny-list constants in zipforms_backend.py:29 and skyslope_backend.py:29, and a docstring in homes/showingtime/showami core/tree.py:15 stating domshell_backend.click / type_text are never imported. For the three browser-backed CLIs the registered groups are fs, page, paths, recipe, recipes, repl and session — no act. Each package's own suite greps its source to keep it so.

finding: The two REST harnesses are GET-only by construction, and the enforcement is a real grep over package source, not a claim. Zoho's single non-GET call is correctly outside the pip package.
evidence: TestGetOnly.FORBIDDEN is a compiled regex over every non-test .py in the package matching requests.(post|put|patch|delete|request|Session), .post(/.put(/.patch(/.delete(, method=, the literals 'POST'/'PUT'/'PATCH'/'DELETE', urllib.request, http.client, httpx, urlopen and Request( — and asserts no match in any file; a second test asserts the set of requests.* names used is a subset of {get, RequestException}. Both pass in zoho (43/43) and lofty (37/37). zoho/tools/mint-access-token.sh lives outside the pip package, POSTs only to ${ACCOUNTS_URL}/oauth/v2/token (the accounts server, never the CRM), parses the response rather than printing it, and prints only the access token — reviewed line by line. TestGetOnly also asserts no .sh file exists inside the package, that the helper passes `bash -n`, that it contains 'oauth/v2/token' and '-X POST', and that it never echoes the client secret or refresh token. The helper has been syntax-checked only and has never run.
fix: None needed. The helper stays unrun until a credential exists — minting a token needs a credential, which is HALT.

The 403 block, its exit code 4 and the click path are stated in all three documents, and all three state plainly that nothing has ever run against Zoho.

finding: One GET-only guard can silently skip. TestGetOnly::test_token_minting_is_outside_the_package calls pytest.skip when it cannot locate tools/mint-access-token.sh — which is the case when the suite runs from site-packages without CLI_ANYTHING_REPO_ROOT set. A suite run that way reports green while one of the read-only guarantees went unchecked.
evidence: tests/test_core.py: the test builds two candidate paths (PKG_DIR.parents[2]/'tools'/... and $CLI_ANYTHING_REPO_ROOT/integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/zoho/tools/...) and does `if helper is None: pytest.skip(...)`. From the source checkout the first candidate resolves and the test PASSES (confirmed — it passed, not skipped, in all 43-passed runs). From an installed copy with the variable unset it would skip. TEST.md Part 2 already instructs running with CLI_ANYTHING_REPO_ROOT set.
fix: Low priority: either fail rather than skip when the package is installed but the repo root is not given, or have the suite assert the skip count is zero. Not changed here — it is a test-hardening call, not a defect, and the guarantee held in every run made in this pass. Noted in TEST.md Part 4 so a green run from site-packages is read correctly.

finding: All seven are PEP 420 namespace packages and coexist in one environment, as designed.
evidence: `find . -path '*/cli_anything/__init__.py'` outside build/ returns nothing — no __init__.py directly under any cli_anything/. In the shared venv, `import cli_anything` yields __file__ of None (a true namespace package) and cli_anything.zoho, .zipforms, .lofty and .skyslope all import cleanly side by side. All seven console scripts install into one bin/ without collision: cli-anything-{homes,lofty,showami,showingtime,skyslope,zipforms,zoho}. Independently verified rather than assumed.
